title: Überlingen midair collision (Bashkirian 2937 / DHL 611)

agencies.name: Bundesstelle für Flugunfalluntersuchung
agencies.report_title: Investigation Report AX001-1-2/02: Collision of Tupolev TU154M and Boeing B757-200 near Überlingen, Lake Constance, 1 July 2002

summary: A Bashkirian Airlines Tu-154M and a DHL Boeing 757-23APF (A9C-DHL) were converging at FL360 at night in Swiss-controlled airspace over southern Germany. The single controller on duty at Skyguide Zurich, working two positions with the short-term conflict alert switched off for maintenance and the telephone system degraded, noticed the conflict late and instructed the Tu-154 to descend. Seconds later TCAS commanded the Tu-154 to climb and the 757 to descend. The Tu-154 crew followed the controller's repeated descent instruction rather than the TCAS RA, and the two aircraft collided at 34,890 ft, killing all 71 people aboard both aircraft.
probable_cause: Immediate causes: the imminent separation infringement was not noticed by ATC in time, and the instruction for the Tu-154M to descend was given at a time when the prescribed separation could no longer be ensured; the Tu-154M crew followed the ATC instruction to descend and continued to do so even after TCAS advised them to climb, so that the manoeuvre was contrary to the TCAS resolution advisory. Systemic causes: the integration of ACAS/TCAS II into the aviation system was insufficient and did not correspond in all points with the system philosophy, with the regulations concerning ACAS/TCAS published by ICAO and the manufacturers being incomplete and partially contradictory; management and quality assurance of the air navigation service company did not ensure that during the night all open workstations were continuously staffed; and management and quality assurance tolerated for years that during times of low traffic flow at night only one controller worked and the other retired to rest.

factors.evidence: Only one controller was on duty at Zurich ACC, handling two workstations and frequencies, while his colleague was resting, as tolerated by Skyguide management.
The Skyguide short-term conflict alert (STCA) optical warning was switched off for maintenance work on the radar system, and the main telephone system was unavailable.
Skyguide management and quality assurance tolerated single-controller night operations and did not ensure safe procedures during system maintenance.

The controller noticed the conflict late, instructed the Tu-154 to descend about 44 seconds before the collision, and repeated the instruction with an incorrect traffic position ('at your 2 o'clock') after TCAS had commanded a climb.
TCAS issued a climb RA to the Tu-154 and a descend RA to the 757 seven seconds after the controller's descent instruction; the Tu-154 crew followed ATC and descended into the 757's descent.
Bashkirian Airlines' TCAS operating documentation and training were ambiguous about the priority of RAs over ATC instructions, reflecting contradictory regulations.
ICAO and manufacturer regulations on TCAS were incomplete and partially contradictory, and Swiss oversight of Skyguide's night staffing was inadequate.
In the Tu-154 cockpit the pilot-in-command in the left seat and the instructor gave conflicting comments about following TCAS or ATC, and the descent was continued.
The collision occurred at night, limiting visual acquisition; the 757 crew and the Tu-154 crew saw each other only seconds before impact.
The 757's vertical fin struck the Tu-154 fuselage at 34,890 ft; both aircraft broke up and fell near Überlingen.

events.text: At Zurich ACC the second controller retires to rest, leaving one controller working both radar positions; the STCA is switched off and the telephone system degraded for maintenance work.
The controller is busy with a delayed Aero Lloyd A320 approach to Friedrichshafen on the second frequency and attempts to telephone Friedrichshafen, without success because of the phone outage.
The Tu-154M at FL360 and the 757 at FL360 converge on crossing tracks about 45 seconds apart; both TCAS systems issue traffic advisories.
Karlsruhe upper area control's STCA alerts its controller, who tries repeatedly to phone Zurich but cannot get through.
Zurich controller instructs the Tu-154 to descend to FL350 expedite because of crossing traffic; the Tu-154 crew begin to descend.
TCAS resolution advisories: 'climb' for the Tu-154 and 'descend' for the 757. The 757 crew follow their RA and descend.
In the Tu-154 the instructor says the controller has told them to descend; the co-pilot notes that TCAS says climb; the descent is continued.
Zurich controller repeats the descent instruction, describing the traffic as at the Tu-154's 2 o'clock position (it was actually to the left); the Tu-154 crew acknowledge and increase the descent.
The 757 crew report to Zurich that they are in a TCAS descent; the transmission is not acknowledged by the controller, who is on the other frequency.
TCAS in the 757 commands 'increase descent'; in the Tu-154 TCAS commands 'increase climb', but the aircraft continues to descend.
The Tu-154 crew see the 757's lights and pull up; the 757 crew see the Tu-154 and push over. Neither manoeuvre is enough.
The two aircraft collide at 34,890 ft at almost a right angle; the 757's fin severs the Tu-154 fuselage. Both aircraft break up and fall near Überlingen; all 71 occupants (69 and 2) killed.

recommendations.text: Change the international requirements so that pilots are required to follow TCAS resolution advisories regardless of contrary ATC instructions, and clarify the regulations and training documentation accordingly.
recommendations.outcome: ICAO amended Annex 2 / PANS-OPS in 2003 to require pilots to follow RAs even when contrary to ATC instructions.

recommendations.text: Develop a TCAS RA downlink so that controllers are informed automatically when an RA has been issued, and modify TCAS logic to reverse an RA if one aircraft does not comply.
recommendations.outcome: TCAS II version 7.1 with RA reversal logic was mandated in Europe; RA downlink via Mode S was developed.

recommendations.text: Ensure that all open workstations at air navigation service units are continuously staffed, that safety-relevant technical work is coordinated with operations, and that conflict alert systems remain operational or the airspace capacity is reduced accordingly.
recommendations.outcome: Skyguide revised its night staffing and maintenance coordination procedures.

recommendations.text: Ensure that TCAS training programmes and operating manuals give unambiguous guidance that RAs take precedence over ATC instructions.

safety_changes: ICAO rule change: TCAS RAs take precedence over ATC instructions; standard phraseology for reporting RAs.
TCAS II version 7.1 with reversal logic and 'level off' advisories mandated in Europe.
Skyguide changes to night staffing, maintenance coordination and safety management; Swiss oversight strengthened.

notes: Record aircraft is the Tu-154M RA-85816 (69 occupants); the other aircraft was DHL Boeing 757-23APF A9C-DHL (2 crew). Occupants and fatalities combine both aircraft.

Key clock times (21:34:42 Karlsruhe STCA, 21:34:49 descent instruction, 21:34:56 RAs, 21:35:03 repeated instruction, 21:35:24 increase descent, 21:35:32 collision) follow the BFU report; earlier times approximate.
